scale.3: Implemented AND tested in last 12 months

Governance & Contract: Board-approved exit strategy exists for every critical/important cloud service
Contract grants termination assistance and an adequate transition period
Contract guarantees data return in open formats with egress fees waived or capped
Provider failure, insolvency, sanction and regulator-order scenarios are covered
Exit triggers (SLA breach, price rise, regulatory order) have a named decision owner
Register of critical services with substitutability assessment is reviewed yearly
Data & Keys: Full export of every tier-1 dataset has been run end-to-end
Backups/replicas exist outside the primary provider's control plane
Encryption keys are held outside the provider (BYOK/HYOK) or re-key is rehearsed
Data formats are open (Parquet, Avro, SQL dumps) with documented schemas
Residency / cross-border transfer constraints for target environments are mapped
Egress volume, duration and cost are modelled from real throughput tests
Architecture: Tier-1 workloads run on containers/VMs with provider-neutral IaC
Proprietary services sit behind an internal adapter/abstraction layer
Identity is federated over OIDC/SAML/SCIM with a provider-independent source of truth
Observability uses open standards (OpenTelemetry) with independent storage
CI/CD and artifact registries do not depend on the cloud being exited
New proprietary services require a documented portability review
Operations & Resilience: A stressed-exit runbook exists per critical service with named owners
A warm or cold target environment exists at a second provider/on-prem for tier-1
Failover to a second provider has been exercised, not just documented
DNS/TTL and network cutover strategy is prepared
SaaS/vendor dependencies hosted on the same cloud are mapped (concentration)
Provider health, financial and geopolitical signals feed the exit triggers
People & Testing: An exit drill or tabletop ran in the last 12 months with tracked findings
Skills in target technologies (Kubernetes, Postgres, Kafka, ...) are maintained
Surge capacity (partners/retainers) is pre-contracted for a stressed exit
Exit-readiness metrics reach the board/risk committee at least annually
A regulator notification and engagement plan is prepared
Lock-in score is tracked over time and drill findings measurably reduce it
